- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70.5) and model holds or rises, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and model forecasts are rising, suppress upward momentum — forecast should not exceed 1.5% above recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust — apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for 2–3 days after sentiment spike.
